messages:
Sam: FYI billing flagged a delta for acme-inc after the rate-smoothing rollout. Looks like retries that trigger tool calls are causing prompt tokens to be charged more than once.

Owen: Can you paste the relevant meter log lines? :eyes:

Sam: Pasted from meter-service for req-9012: 
```
REQ=req-9012 attempt=1 reserve=140 prompt=110 completion=22 charge=132
REQ=req-9012 attempt=2 reserve=140 prompt=110 completion=28 charge=158
// meter reported total charge: 290
// expected canonical charge: prompt(110) + last completion(28) = 138
```

Maria: Hmm. Why is the prompt repeated across attempts? We should only count the prompt once per top-level request. :thinking:

Tashi: My read: we reserve prompt tokens on start (reserve_on_start=true). When a retry happens due to a tool runtime or transport hiccup we emit a new meter event for the child completion but the child doesn't carry the top-level idempotency context. Meter sees two distinct consumption events.

Priya: That matches why Console shows different numbers for the same timeframe. Console aggregates by client_request_id and collapses children; billing uses raw meter events and has no parent pointer.

Sam: Right now child meter events lack parent_request_id or parent_request_fingerprint. No way to authoritative-dedupe.

Owen: Proposed approaches: 
  1) Propagate a parent identifier across toolcall boundaries (SDK/runtime sets X-Parent-Request-ID) and make meter-service dedupe when parent is present.
  2) Change reservation/finalization: reserve prompt on start but only finalize (commit) counts once the top-level request finishes; release on error/timeouts.

Tashi: Option 1 is faster and lower-risk operationally. Option 2 is safer long-term but touches billing finalize flows and has more rollback complexity.

Priya: For Option 1 we need to ensure external connectors and older runtimes can carry the header. We'll add a lightweight compatibility shim: runtime injects header, fallback: client_request_id + prompt fingerprint correlation.

Sam: Short-term hotfix plan: 
 - implement a heuristic in meter-service: if an incoming prompt token charge matches an existing recent prompt fingerprint for same org+client_request_id within 120s, suppress duplicate prompt charge (log and emit metric).
 - medium-term: propagate X-Parent-Request-ID in all internal toolcall paths and update meter-service to dedupe by parent_id as authoritative.
 - Console: add a toggle in the tokens breakdown UI labeled "Include retries (billing view)" and explain the difference.

Owen: SDK/runtime pseudocode for propagation: 
```
// caller side when invoking a tool from the request context
headers["X-Parent-Request-ID"] = ctx.request_id
// child meter event includes meter.parent_request_id = headers["X-Parent-Request-ID"]
```

Tashi: I'll own the hotfix PR for the heuristic and the metric instrumentation. Opening draft now.

Infra-bot: deploy-bot: quota-meter-hotfix branch built and queued for staging (build-214) :white_check_mark:

Priya: I'll mock the Console toggle and begin copy for the billing docs explaining prompt vs completion vs retry accounting.

Sam: QA: add regression in billing/qa harness to simulate (a) transport retry, (b) tool-triggered retry. Assert final invoice equals expected single-prompt charge.

Maria: Create a public-facing note template for customers we contact. We should be transparent about why Console and Billing may differ during rollout windows.

Sam: Ticket created: ENG-4829 "Deduplicate prompt charges across toolcall retries". Owners: Tashi (eng-platform), Priya (frontend/console), Sam (billing QA).

Owen: Can infra notify connector partners to start sending X-Parent-Request-ID next week? We'll include migration instructions.

Tashi: Draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-platform/pull/981 (WIP). Hotfix to staging today, prod tomorrow morning after smoke test.

Maria: Thanks all. Once hotfix lands, we should reconcile invoices for the impacted window and contact acme-inc proactively if bill changes >3%.

Sam: I'll monitor and post a follow-up here with snapshots.

Owen: Great. Keeping thread open for any fallout. :+1:
